verdict.rationale: Gazebo's own docs describe official libraries that developers use directly in their own C++ applications: gz-math, sdformat, gz-transport, and a C++ client library for Fuel. The gz-sim repo ships example standalone programs that use gz-sim as a library, plus a documented plugin development path. Missing for 10: evidence of SDKs beyond C++ (e.g. Python bindings), in-depth API reference documentation, and independent or hands-on corroboration of building against the libraries.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can build against official SDKs

citations.quote: For those who use individual Gazebo libraries (like gz-math, sdformat, or gz-transport) directly in their own C++ applications
A C++ client library and command line tools for interacting with Gazebo Fuel servers
Example standalone programs that use gz-sim as a library.
Develop custom plugins for robot, sensor, and environment control.
